fixes.explanation: Cherubim, skillfully worked right into the linen. God says it again for the veil, "…with cherubim skillfully worked into it." (Exodus 26:31). Those curtains and that veil were works of art, and I'm over here proud when my stamp comes out straight.

That's a fair thought, friend, but the text goes another way. The fifty gold clasps join the two sets of five curtains, and God gives the reason: "…so that the tabernacle will be a unit." (Exodus 26:6). Two sets go in and one tabernacle comes out.

Yes! God says to "…place the ark of the Testimony behind the veil." The veil then separates the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place (Exodus 26:33). The ark gets the room behind the veil, and the mercy seat goes on top of it (Exodus 26:34).

That name isn't in this passage, friend. The Bible does mention an upper room in Acts 1:13, but it has nothing to do with this tent. Here, God says the veil separates the Holy Place from "…the Most Holy Place." (Exodus 26:33).

God does put the ark of the Testimony behind the veil, with the mercy seat on top (Exodus 26:33-34). But the table and the lampstand aren't placed back there. They go outside the veil, the table on the north side and the lampstand opposite it on the south (Exodus 26:35).

I do love a bell, friend. Ruby, one of my cookie cutter kids, is one, and I remember how you could hear her from across the kitchen. But the altar doesn't get bells. God says to make a horn on each of its four corners, all one piece with the altar.

Bronze it is. The altar is overlaid with bronze, and God says, "Make all its utensils of bronze…" (Exodus 27:2-3). The grate is bronze mesh with bronze rings, and the poles are acacia wood overlaid with bronze (Exodus 27:4, 6). Even the tent pegs are bronze (Exodus 27:19). That's a lot of bronze, and I love the consistency.

Silver is in there, but not here. It's on the bases under the wall frames, and on the hooks and bands of the courtyard posts (Exodus 26:19; 27:17). The altar is overlaid with bronze, and its utensils are made of bronze (Exodus 27:2-3).

That's the word. God says the Israelites are to bring pure oil of pressed olives for the light, "…to keep the lamps burning continually." (Exodus 27:20). It's an instruction for all the time, not just some of it. I'd want that rule for my own oven light too.
That's right. God says, "…Aaron and his sons are to tend the lamps before the LORD…" (Exodus 27:21). Aaron is Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14). So the lamp job stays in the family.

The elders aren't given this job, friend. God says, "…Aaron and his sons are to tend the lamps before the LORD…" (Exodus 27:21). Aaron is Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), and he and his sons get the assignment.
